stem:
Meena notices that the dal in her pressure cooker cooks faster on some days than on others.

Her teacher says that a curiosity becomes a scientific question only when it is focused enough to guide careful observation, a fair experiment, and a clear explanation.

Which row shows a question that has been made scientific and a matching way to test it?

options.text: question: Why is cooking dal so interesting?; test: think about it during dinner
question: Does dal cook faster with more water or less water?; test: cook equal masses of dal with different measured volumes of water, keeping the flame and time the same
question: Why do all spices do things in food?; test: read a recipe book
question: What is the best dal in the world?; test: ask friends which dal they like

tables: {"headers":["question","test"],"rows":[["Why is cooking dal so interesting?","think about it during dinner"],["Does dal cook faster with more water or less water?","cook equal masses of dal with different measured volumes of water, keeping the flame and time the same"],["Why do all spices do things in food?","read a recipe book"],["What is the best dal in the world?","ask friends which dal they like"]],"row_labels":["A","B","C","D"],"caption":"","is_option_table":true}

teacher.key_rationale: Row B pairs a focused, testable question (one variable changed: volume of water) with a fair experiment that controls other conditions (same dal mass, flame, time), so it can guide observation, experimentation and explanation. Rows A, C and D are unfocused or opinion-based and their 'tests' involve no controlled investigation.
